research_question: What is the effect of extended-duration anticoagulation, compared with standard-duration anticoagulation, on major bleeding within 45 days (short-term) in acutely ill medical patients receiving venous thromboembolism prophylaxis?
outcome_description: Incidence of major bleeding events occurring within 45 days (short-term) from primary analysis.
positive_direction: Lower risk of major bleeding in the extended-duration anticoagulation group compared to the standard-duration group (extended duration is safer).
search_queries: extended duration thromboprophylaxis acutely ill medical randomized trial
extended anticoagulation standard duration venous thromboembolism major bleeding comparison
extended versus standard duration thromboprophylaxis medical patients bleeding outcome
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials or comparative empirical studies in acutely ill hospitalized medical patients receiving thromboprophylaxis.
Direct comparison of extended-duration anticoagulation versus standard-duration anticoagulation (or standard followed by placebo).
Quantitative reporting of primary analysis major bleeding events within 45 days post-randomization.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, commentaries, or study protocols).
No comparison between an extended-duration anticoagulation arm and a standard-duration anticoagulation (or placebo post-standard) arm.
No quantitative outcome data on short-term (<= 45 days) major bleeding events enabling calculation of risk ratios.
Completely unrelated to venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in acutely ill hospitalized medical patients (e.g., surgical, orthopedic, or outpatient non-medical populations).
moderators_to_extract: Anticoagulant drug class in extended arm (e.g., DOAC vs LMWH)
Specific agent (e.g., rivaroxaban, betrixaban, apixaban, enoxaparin)
effect_size_note: Dichotomous major bleeding event counts and randomized sample sizes pooled as Risk Ratio (RR). Major bleeding is a harm outcome. Trials with zero events in both arms are treated as not estimable and excluded from ratio-based pooling rather than applying continuity corrections.
